brief.headline: Konstantinovka falls; Ukrainian drones hammer St. Petersburg, Crimea
brief.lead: Pro-Kremlin channels celebrated the claimed capture of Konstantinovka as the war's dominant story, while an unusually anxious counter-narrative emerged around Ukrainian long-range drone strikes on St. Petersburg oil terminals, Leningrad region, and a Crimean fuel crisis.

developments.title: Channels declare Konstantinovka captured, eye Slavyansk
developments.body: All monitored channels claimed Russian forces liberated Konstantinovka, described as Donbas's seventh-largest administrative center with 150km of trenches and 20 defense districts. Kotsnews and WarGonzo cite Putin framing it as a first phase, with Slavyansk reportedly 8km away; Sladkov+ claims 13,000 Ukrainian losses. Claims unconfirmed and largely MoD-echoed.

developments.title: Ukrainian drones strike St. Petersburg, Leningrad region
developments.body: Channels reported a Ukrainian strike on a St. Petersburg oil terminal and 67 drones downed over Leningrad region, with debris near Vysotsk port. Russian MoD claimed 389 drones destroyed overnight nationwide. The negative tone marks a sharp mood swing (net -86) on this topic.

developments.title: Crimea fuel crisis and refinery damage acknowledged
developments.body: Two Majors reported a Crimean fuel crisis from Ukrainian strikes on fuel infrastructure, with official refueling halted, and claimed Ukrainian drones disabled 42.74% of Russian refinery capacity and 60+ fuel storage tanks over the past month — a rare admission of systemic damage. Figures channel-sourced and unverified.

developments.title: Kharkiv advances claimed near Volchansk
developments.body: Rybar, Two Majors and Kotsnews reported the Northern grouping capturing Losevka and Zemlyanoy Yar south of Volchansk and approaching the Belyy Kolodiets line; Kotsnews adds four more settlements in Kharkiv region. Claims unconfirmed.

developments.title: West framed as escalating drone war on Russia
developments.body: Rybar highlighted NATO counter-drone exercises (WATT26 in Latvia with Ukrainian firms), Japan-Ukraine drone manufacturing clusters, and Moldova closing Russia's Kishinev cultural center. Two Majors alleged Finland closed Gulf airspace to aid Ukrainian strikes. West & NATO sentiment fell to net -88.

developments.title: Nord Stream, Monaco bombing pinned on Kyiv
developments.body: WarGonzo amplified German prosecutors charging Ukrainian SBU officer Kuznetsov over the Nord Stream bombing, and separately linked a Monaco car-bombing of businessman Yermolayev to a Kyiv sanctions list, advancing a 'Ukrainian terror in Europe' narrative.

narrative_watch.title: Drone war as existential cost driver
narrative_watch.body: Channels increasingly frame drone warfare as an escalating, expensive attritional burden requiring integrated air defense, migrating from triumphalism toward candid anxiety about rear-area vulnerability.

narrative_watch.title: 'Ukrainian terror in Europe'
narrative_watch.body: WarGonzo's push linking Kyiv to the Monaco bombing and Nord Stream charges builds a frame casting Ukraine as a terror sponsor across Europe.

narrative_watch.title: Moldova/Transnistria as next flashpoint
narrative_watch.body: Two Majors and Rybar recycle the frame that EU-funded armored vehicles and NATO training prepare Moldova to seize Transnistria.

mood_lines.text: Euphoric (net +100) over Konstantinovka's claimed fall and Kharkiv advances, with channels already pointing toward Slavyansk.
Upbeat on drone strikes hitting Ukrainian fuel infrastructure, highways and a poultry farm framed as export-funding targets.
Sharp negative swing (net -86); alarm over St. Petersburg terminal, Leningrad drones and Crimea fuel crisis.
Deteriorating (net -88); NATO drone exercises, Japan-Ukraine cluster and Moldova moves cast as coordinated escalation.
Mixed; anxiety on drone defense and espionage balanced by Africa Corps wins in Mali and air-defense tech touts.
Uniformly negative; jabs at A Just Russia's late Donbas support and mockery of Zelenskyy's Konstantinovka challenge.

flag_texts.title: Ukraine strikes on Russia plunges to net -86
flag_texts.body: Sustained negative posting on the St. Petersburg oil terminal strike, 67+ drones over Leningrad region and a Crimean fuel crisis drove sentiment sharply down, including a rare admission that 42.74% of refinery capacity was hit.

flag_texts.title: West & NATO sinks to net -88 (down 41)
flag_texts.body: Coverage of NATO counter-drone exercises, Japan-Ukraine drone manufacturing, Moldova's cultural-center closure and alleged Finnish airspace collusion drove a steep negative shift in West-focused sentiment.

flag_texts.title: Mobilisation and Putin-criticism watchlist quiet
flag_texts.body: Despite the day's frontline triumphalism, monitored channels ran no mobilisation rumours or direct criticism of Putin; internal grievance instead targeted A Just Russia and bureaucratic barriers for veterans.
